findings.issue: Known forward-limitation (spec is silent, so recording as forward, not blocking): the owner's mgmt-grant scope and the genesis assignment org_scope are an org-set over the three CURRENT roots {fin,cs,plat}. A NEW root department created later (another parent_id NULL node) is NOT covered by this set — the owner's authority would not automatically reach it, because isNarrowerOrEqual(newRoot, {fin,cs,plat}) is false (a sibling root is not ⊑ any member). The ADR §3 chose the org-set over synthesizing a super-root (correctly, to honor additive-only AC-17), but the consequence is that forest-wide owner reach is pinned to the seeded 3-root snapshot. This matches the dev-silo N=1 reality and the spec's 'tenant-root org node ... covers every subtree' is satisfied for the current forest; the gap only appears if the org tree grows a new root. Out of scope for T-0029 (no new-root flow exists yet); the structural-grant editor / write-API is T-0030, which is the natural place to re-broaden owner scope when a root is added.
findings.suggestion: No code change for T-0029. Carry forward to T-0030 (write-API) / T-0053 (live getGrants): when a new root department is minted, either re-issue the owner's mgmt-grant org-set to include it, or revisit the super-root decision. Recommend a one-line forward-note in the ADR's forest-root seam section so the limitation is explicit for the sibling tasks.
